chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Sabir, the mawla of Bassam, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) led us in the Maghrib prayer, and he recited the two Mu'awwidhat (Chapters 113 and 114), then said: 'These two are from the Quran.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ: The two Surahs of seeking refuge (al-Falaq and an-Nas)

ai.seo_question: Are the Mu'awwidhat (Surah al-Falaq and Surah an-Nas) considered part of the Quran?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) recited Surah al-Falaq and Surah an-Nas during the Maghrib prayer to demonstrate their practical usage in worship. He explicitly affirmed that they are part of the Quran, a key point of discussion in Shia jurisprudence regarding whether they are verses of the Quran (*ayat min al-Qur'an*) or distinct supplications (*du'a*) with Quranic authority. This establishes their status as canonical recitations for both prayer and protection.
